title: C: Immutable Collections (Simulated)
description: Implement a simple immutable persistent data structure: a persistent stack where each push creates a new stack sharing structure with the old one.

steps.title: Persistent Stack
steps.description: Define a `PStack` node with value and a pointer to the next node (the previous version). Write `PStack* pstack_push(PStack *old, int val)` that creates a new node pointing to old. Write `int pstack_peek(PStack *s)` and `PStack* pstack_pop(PStack *s)`. Demonstrate that old versions remain valid after push.
hints: Nodes are singly-linked and never modified.
push: alloc new node with next=old.
Old stack still exists after push.

verification.failureMessage: Old versions should remain valid after push
